verdict.rationale: Obsidian's docs say notes are plain-text Markdown files stored locally, usable offline, under your control, and syncable through Git, Dropbox, iCloud, OneDrive and other third-party services instead of Obsidian Sync. A community user confirms running it fully local with their own storage sync for de-Googling. However, there is no first-party self-hostable sync server, and a community report says Git-based sync is weak for multi-device sync and collaboration. Vendor-only features like Sync collaboration and Publish have no self-hosted equivalent. Missing for 10: an official self-hosted sync backend, evidence that self-operated sync (e.g. Git) works reliably across devices and for collaboration.
